facts.text: Lowrey takes its name from Major George Lowrey, a key Cherokee statesman and assistant principal chief during the mid-nineteenth century.
Lowrey was incorporated into the Cherokee Nation's territory following the forced relocation of the Cherokee people during the Trail of Tears.
Lowrey evolved gradually as an unincorporated rural community within Cherokee lands rather than being developed as a planned townsite.
Lowrey sits within the Illinois River watershed as part of the Ozark Plateau foothills in northeastern Oklahoma.
Forested landscapes of oak-hickory associations dominate the thin, rocky soils found throughout the Lowrey area.
Lowrey experiences a humid subtropical climate influenced by warm, moist air flowing from the Gulf of Mexico.
